releases.headline: The full sniper doctrine now belongs to every purple tank.

Lineage-Wide Sniper Doctrine: Marksman, Railgun, Ghost, Singularity, Prism Rail, Specter and Assassin all use the Forward Observer reconnaissance model for long-range target authorization.
All purple AI tanks are restricted to ordinary 720-unit direct hull vision; targets beyond that require a live observer relay rather than privileged sniper sight.
The non-beam purple classes now require continuous class-specific precision dwell before long-range fire instead of firing immediately when generic aim alignment succeeds.
Losing the target, breaking the firing cadence, losing remote authorization, or suffering accurate suppression cancels non-beam precision preparation.
Distinct Purple Mastery: Marksman uses a deliberate sight picture with a 0.42-second remote precision dwell and a meaningful post-shot reveal/recovery window.
Ghost uses a faster 0.34-second ambush dwell and shorter reveal, preserving cloak-and-relocate identity rather than becoming a slower Railgun.
Specter uses the fastest 0.24-second precision cycle and short recovery, rewarding rapid phase positioning and repeated angle creation.
Assassin uses the longest 0.54-second precision commitment and strongest non-beam reveal/recovery cost to support its brutal alpha-strike identity.
Within direct sight, non-beam precision dwell is shorter so purple tanks remain responsive when opponents successfully close distance.
Warning, Suppression and Projectiles: Marksman, Ghost, Specter and Assassin now provide two-stage directional pre-shot audio and screen-edge threat cues when preparing distant attacks against the player.
Class-flavored SIGHT LOCK, AMBUSH LOCK, HUNT LOCK and EXEC LOCK cues communicate late commitment without exposing exact shooter coordinates.
Accurate hits or near-miss suppression can break non-beam sniper preparation, extending the same read/respond/punish principle beyond Rail weapons.
Non-beam sniper rounds receive restrained violet motion trails and real near-player flyby audio so fast precision fire remains readable while in flight.
Committed non-beam shots briefly reveal their firing bearing, creating an earned advance or punish window.
Observer Counterplay: Destroying the active Forward Observer now disables long-range observer relay for about 3.4 seconds instead of allowing another escort to restore remote targeting immediately.
During observer-relay reboot, the sniper can still fight through ordinary direct sight but cannot use spare-drone remote contacts for distant target authorization.
Player purple tanks receive OBSERVER DOWN / OBSERVER LINK RESTORED feedback and a short relay-reboot countdown.
Rail-Specific Identity Preserved: Railgun, Singularity and Prism Rail retain their deeper focus-to-fire and quick-shot mechanics, explicit Rail projectile integrity, swept projectile interception and beam-specific feedback.
Violet Doctrine deliberately shares reconnaissance, finite acquisition, warning, suppression and punishability across the lineage without homogenizing every purple weapon into a Railgun.

releases.headline: Snipers need eyes before they can kill beyond sight.

Sniper AI: Replaced the sniper lineage's generic AI combat loop with a dedicated tracking/firing model that uses sampled target motion, finite turret turn rates, aim commitment, and continuous focus instead of instant reacquisition.
Rail focus can no longer remain banked while an AI loses alignment or target intent; losing aim, target authorization, suppression, or spotter contact cancels the stored charge.
AI Railguns now need roughly 0.82 seconds of continuous qualified focus for a normal full shot (0.70 seconds for elite AI) and receive a post-shot recovery floor before another full attack cycle.
Long-range sniper targeting is no longer granted through the generic AI vision bonus. Sniper hull vision is deliberately limited; distant targets require a live spotter contact.
Spotter Drones: The first drone in each sniper squad becomes a Forward Observer with an extended patrol leash, deliberate wide orbit, and its own rotating field-of-view cone.
Spotters patrol away from the sniper, opportunistically destroy nearby map shapes, and independently scan tanks inside their own field of view.
A valid spotter sighting grants only a short-lived contact relay; destroy the spotter or leave its view and the sniper loses distant target authorization after the contact memory expires.
Player snipers receive readable SPOT contact information from their observer without automatic aiming; enemy spotters are visually identifiable and therefore attackable counterplay.
Warning and Counterplay: Being acquired by an enemy spotter now produces a distinct SPOTTED cue before the sniper firing sequence begins.
Enemy Rail focus against the player now has two directional pre-shot warning stages, a stronger mobile-readable edge glint, and a RAIL FOCUS cue before full release.
Rail rounds now trigger an actual near-player flyby crack based on their flight path, so the in-flight sound is no longer only a firing-time effect.
Sniper AI must rotate and maintain its committed aim before firing, preserving movement feints and suppression as real counterplay.
Evolution and Safety: Opening an evolution milestone clears hostile banked Rail focus before the game pauses.

Completing or dismissing an evolution/perk/gene choice grants a short spawn-shield grace period, clears stale firing input, and forces enemy snipers to reacquire rather than firing immediately as the menu disappears.
The stat-upgrade tray is automatically minimized after evolution choices so it cannot strand the player behind a large mobile UI panel when combat resumes.
Drone and Stability Fixes: Controller drone state now receives a defensive invariant pass for invalid positions, stale targets, broken dash vectors, impossible phases, and corrupt Command Nodes.
Invalid Controller drone states recover to a safe formation state instead of remaining stuck or propagating NaN movement through the swarm.
Runtime JavaScript syntax checks and release-JSON validation are now part of the GitHub materialization workflow before the playable page is regenerated.

releases.headline: Sniper and Controller mastery gets a full feedback pass.

Sniper Polish: Rail focus now gains a segmented reticle, live charge percentage, a clear FOCUS READY state, a restrained lock-ready sound, and tiny supported-device haptic confirmation.
Rail projectiles receive longer luminous motion trails and brighter spear-like cores so hypervelocity shots are easier to read without slowing them down.

Projectile interception now produces dedicated metallic/electromagnetic impact feedback, brighter collision blooms, and a RAIL DENIED confirmation when the player successfully destroys an incoming Rail round.
Controller Polish: The active Command Node now previews the current formation geometry instead of behaving as only a destination marker.
A compact node status ring shows how many drones are linked and whether the squad is forming, arming, diving, or recovering.
Committed hostile drone dives aimed at the player gain a longer restrained trajectory cue for better small-screen readability without exposing pre-commit prediction.
Breaking a winding-up enemy dive now gives a distinct DIVE BROKEN confirmation and dedicated interruption sound.
Successful near-miss dodges against committed AI drone runs now produce a restrained EVADED cue, flyby sound, ring, and tiny haptic confirmation.
Successful drone impacts gain heavier impact audio, flash feedback, and small context-sensitive camera response.
Sound and Feel: Added layered focus-ready, Rail interception, drone impact, drone interruption, and drone near-miss procedural SFX with stereo placement where applicable.
Feedback is deliberately event-driven and throttled so the richer soundscape communicates important combat state without turning swarm battles into constant noise.
Mobile haptics remain short and selective: full focus readiness, Rail denial, hostile drone impact, and close committed-dive evasion.
Technical: Signal Bloom is a presentation/QoL patch layered after Silent Horizon and Second Body, preserving their mechanics and existing two-stick control grammar.
The polish runtime passes JavaScript syntax validation before deployment.

Controls and Command: Controller aim now commands a visible Swarm Command Node while the hull remains on the movement stick.
Right-stick direction chooses the swarm bearing, stick depth controls deployment distance, and releasing aim recalls the squadron.
Desktop uses the same language: hold fire to command toward the cursor, cursor distance controls deployment depth, and release recalls.
Autonomy handles shape farming; serious PvP pressure now requires active command instead of nearest-target autopilot.
Combat and Counterplay: Controller gun hits DESIGNATE an enemy for a short coordination window, rewarding aim without creating permanent lock-on.
Commanded drones establish formation geometry before attacking instead of walking directly into the nearest enemy.
Attack runs now have readable wind-up, a late trajectory commitment, high-speed dive, overshoot, and recovery phases.

A defender can movement-feint before commitment, dodge after the dive locks, shoot a winding-up drone to cancel its run, destroy drones, or exploit the Controller hull while the swarm is overextended.
A launched dive cannot be recalled mid-flight; pre-launch attacks can be recalled, making commitment meaningful for both sides.
Drone dashes use swept collision so high-speed attack runs do not miss solely because of frame alignment.
Lineage Mastery: Drone Carrier uses a responsive three-drone wedge for learning command depth and attack timing.
Overlord establishes a six-drone far-side crescent to create encirclement pressure and alternating attack angles.
Warden and Citadel form movable phalanx lines whose real drone hulls can physically screen firing lanes; Bulwark tightens their response.
Hivemind arranges nine hunters in a rotating ring, turning spacing and cascading attack timing into its mastery problem.
Broodmother forms twin attack claws and preferentially commits damaged or temporary brood, making attrition and sacrifice tactically useful.
Valkyrie uses a fast cavalry wing with the shortest wind-up, fastest dives, and shortest recovery, increasing both execution ceiling and punishability.
AI and Feedback: AI Controllers use the same Command Node, formation, wind-up, trajectory lock, dive, recovery, and drone-health rules as the player.
Normal AI uses less prediction and slower command tracking while elite AI earns strength through better positioning rather than impossible execution.
New procedural command, recall, designation, drone wind-up, and launch sounds make swarm intent easier to read.
The player sees a command tether, engagement zone, off-screen command marker, designation reticle, attack wind-up rings, committed dive vectors, and dash trails.
A short Controller tutorial appears on evolution: command direction, analog deployment depth, recall, and designation all use the existing NOVA controls.

releases.headline: Snipers become lethal, readable skill duels.

Sniper Gameplay: Railgun, Singularity and Prism Rail focus before a full-power shot.
Release early for a weaker quick-shot under pressure.
Deep focus increasingly commits turret aim, enabling movement feints and counter-baits.
Committed shots create recovery windows opponents can use to take ground.
Counterplay: Off-screen committed snipers reveal approximate bearing through a restrained edge glint and directional audio, not exact coordinates.
Accurate suppression can break deep focus while random distant spray remains inefficient.
Rail rounds use explicit interception durability instead of inheriting excessive toughness from penetration.
Swept projectile collision prevents hypervelocity Rail rounds tunneling through correctly placed defensive fire.
Sound and Feedback: Synthesized focus whine, Rail discharge, quick-shot report and incoming sonic crack.
Restrained mobile haptics for dangerous off-screen committed shots where supported.
AI snipers obey the same focus and commitment language as players.

Drones: Introduced combat drones as persistent arena entities.
Controller builds gained hunter swarms as a distinct combat identity.
Drones gained their own hull health, targeting, respawning and combat behavior.

Foundation: Initial playable release of NOVA TANKS.
